purpose: Hourly authoritative-vendor integration/value delta. Adds Siemens Insights Hub as a distinct industrial-IoT source and Schneider EcoStruxure Resource Advisor as a distinct energy-cost source whose customer integration transport is not yet evidenced. No vendor tenant credentials were used and connector writes remain disabled.

systems.name: Siemens Insights Hub
systems.evidenceNote: Siemens documents RESTful Insights Hub Industrial IoT APIs and SDK clients for Asset Management, IoT Time Series, Time Series Aggregates, IoT File, MindConnect and related services. Time-series reads can page via Link headers; service/API versions differ across SDKs and older versions are retained for backward compatibility before deprecation. MindConnect supports upstream upload of time series, events, files and asset data models with documented quotas, but that does not imply SFTP or webhook semantics for the WFM read connector: the proven WFM integration path here is the documented REST API family. Technical access can use application or tenant service credentials to obtain tokens. Several services also expose mutative endpoints, so the WFM connector is strictly read-only and must use operation-level permission enforcement rather than assume a named Siemens access tier is read-only. No tenant or sandbox authentication was attempted.

requiredPermissions: tenant/application technical identity limited to required read APIs
read Asset Management metadata needed for asset/work-centre mapping
read IoT Time Series/TS Aggregates and event/file data through documented read APIs only where required
no time-series, asset, file, event, device, agent or management-plane writes
tenant/site data scope restricted to the customer's approved manufacturing assets
dataAvailableOrExpected: industrial asset hierarchy and aspect metadata
machine events such as failures/emergency stops where customers publish them
asset-linked files and device/log artefacts where authorised
agent-side asset data models and measurement mappings
automationOpportunities: machine-stop/recovery signals can trigger labour redeployment and recall recommendations
correlate staffed time with machine state and production telemetry by work centre
use aggregate time-series reads for efficient shift/day performance correlation instead of high-volume raw polling
detect stale or interrupted telemetry before using machine state in workforce decisions
combine energy-like measurements published as time series with labour/production outcomes when the customer supplies trustworthy tag semantics
customerValue: faster integration where Siemens Insights Hub is already the industrial data layer
savingsHypotheses: reduce paid idle labour by responding earlier to machine failures and recovery
reduce bespoke plant integration effort by consuming the customer's existing Insights Hub asset model
reduce telemetry-processing cost and API load by using aggregates for long-range workforce analysis
identify staffing conditions associated with throughput loss or repeated downtime
dataGaps: worker identity, employment, payroll and roster truth normally remain in HCM/WFM/payroll systems
asset/aspect names and tag semantics are customer-specific and require canonical mapping
not every tenant exposes the same services, versions, regions or licensed capabilities
event availability depends on what plant agents and upstream systems publish
constraintsRisks: time-series reads can require pagination through response Link headers
API versions differ between services/SDKs and older versions have deprecation paths, so capability negotiation and schema fingerprints are required
vendor quotas, call-rate limits and time-window limits require bounded polling, backoff and aggregate selection
late/out-of-order data and millisecond timestamp precision must be handled without corrupting shift attribution
technical client secrets are version/tenant sensitive and must remain executor-boundary only
Siemens access labels must not be treated as proof of read-only semantics; some limited access modes can still manage assets/files or create events
write/delete endpoints exist and remain prohibited until separate sandbox write-roundtrip evidence and customer authorisation
direct plant-network access remains prohibited; WFM reads the governed cloud/edge data layer rather than scanning PLC networks
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Build an Insights Hub thin adapter on the existing REST profile with service/version capability discovery, Link-header pagination, quota-aware retries, timestamp/order normalization and canonical asset/aspect mapping. Then obtain an authorised Siemens development/customer tenant for least-privilege authentication and a read round-trip before any write path is considered.

systems.name: Schneider Electric EcoStruxure Resource Advisor
systems.evidenceNote: Schneider Electric documents Resource Advisor as a cloud platform aggregating enterprise energy and sustainability data, including utility-bill validation, energy cost/budget analysis, interval consumption and site-level benchmarking. This verifies a high-value data opportunity but the public product documentation reviewed does not establish a supported customer API, authentication method, webhook, SFTP or file-export contract. The system intentionally has no protocol assigned until an authoritative integration interface or authorised tenant/export sample is available; this is an explicit integration gap rather than an inferred connector path.

requiredPermissions: customer-authorised read access to energy/resource data only after an interface is identified
site/entity scope limited to WFM cost and optimisation use cases
no BMS/control permission and no procurement mutation authority
automationOpportunities: attribute verified energy spend and consumption to site/shift alongside labour and production
identify staffed non-productive periods with abnormal energy consumption
alert on energy-cost or consumption drift before shift-cost variance becomes material
combine tariff/cost context with staffing and production forecasts when customer-authorised data is available
customerValue: less manual utility-bill and energy-data reconciliation
executive site-level cost and sustainability reporting
savingsHypotheses: identify energy consumed during paid but non-productive time
reduce spreadsheet effort reconciling utility bills, sites and shift outcomes
improve start-up/shutdown staffing decisions using interval energy profiles
surface tariff/budget exposure alongside labour-cost forecasts
dataGaps: public product documentation reviewed does not establish a supported external API, webhook, SFTP or file-export contract for customer integration
tariff, invoice and procurement fields depend on customer licensing, geography and configured data services
workforce identity and production-order detail must come from other systems
constraintsRisks: do not infer API availability from the platform's ability to aggregate data
energy and procurement data can cross legal entities/countries and requires explicit site/entity/data-residency scoping
any BMS/control surface must remain segregated from the Resource Advisor WFM read path
do not reuse generic EcoStruxure BMS protocols as evidence for the separate Resource Advisor cloud product
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Obtain Schneider/customer Resource Advisor interface documentation or an authorised tenant/export sample; only then assign an existing REST/file/middleware protocol path and prove a read round-trip. Until then, treat Resource Advisor as a verified value source with an unresolved transport boundary, not as an available connector.
